name: KineticHub Frontend Doctor
author: kinetichub

sections.description:
Something on the page scrolls sideways. A sticky header stops sticking. A button
will not take a click. Frontend Doctor looks at the page as your browser has
actually laid it out, and shows you the element responsible.

It runs entirely in your browser, on the page you are already looking at.
Nothing is uploaded, nothing is stored, and nothing is sent anywhere. There is
no scan history, no dashboard of scores, and no database table – close the panel
and the plugin has left no trace but the file it was installed from.

Five checks

  • Viewport Doctor – finds the element making the page scroll sideways.
  • Sticky Doctor – explains why a sticky header or sidebar is not sticking.
  • Click Doctor – finds what is sitting on top of a button and swallowing the click.
  • Floating UI Inspector – finds floating buttons, bars and widgets sitting on top of each other.
  • Anchor Doctor – checks in-page links and where they actually land.

Built to stay out of the way

Only administrators see it. A logged-out visitor loads none of it – not a byte,
not a tag, not a request. An administrator browsing their own site carries a
launcher of well under two kilobytes, and the diagnostic engine is fetched only
when they ask for it.

Rebuilding the compiled JavaScript

The two files in assets/js are compiled. Everything they are compiled from
ships beside them, in assets/src, along with the script that compiles them.

With Node.js 18 or newer, in the plugin directory:

  1. npm install – installs one dependency, the esbuild bundler.
  2. npm run build

That rewrites assets/js/khfd-launcher.js and assets/js/khfd-runtime.js from
assets/src. The build is deterministic: on an unmodified copy of the plugin it
reproduces the two shipped files byte for byte.

The human-readable JavaScript source is in assets/src, and scripts/build.js
rebuilds the two compiled bundles from it; both ship in this package. The
public source repository contains the same source and the build material needed
to rebuild the distributed JavaScript. The internal test suites, linters and
release tooling are not part of this package or of the public source
repository.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin to /wp-content/plugins/, or install it through the
    Plugins screen.
  2. Activate it.
  3. Visit any page on your site and choose Scan This Page in the admin bar,
    or open Tools -> Frontend Doctor.
sections.faq:
Does anything leave my site?

No. The scan runs in your browser. The plugin makes no network request of its
own, has no REST route, no admin-ajax endpoint, and no analytics.

Does it store anything?

No. It creates no options, no transients, no user meta and no database tables.

Can editors use it?

No. It requires the manage_options capability, which in practice means
administrators.

Will it change my site?

No. It reads the page and draws on top of it. It never writes to your content,
never applies a fix, and never modifies the layout it is measuring.
